title: RADAR: Acquisition-Adversarial Attention Pooling over a Frozen Chest-Radiograph Foundation Model for Tuberculosis Screening

figures.caption:
RADAR. One frozen encoder, weights shared across passes, reads the lung crop and the full
frame at $518$\,px and the lung crop again at $700$\,px. Patch tokens from blocks $3,6,9,12$ are
pooled by a learned tuberculosis query in each head group. The three $518$\,px groups each read
both views and fuse them in probability space at $\lambda_c=0.90$ before the weighted sum; the
$700$\,px group is Platt-mapped and enters at $\omega=0.15$. Every constant is that of Eq.~(5).
Blue is frozen, orange is trained.}
\label{fig:arch
figures.label: fig:arch

figures.caption:
Both panels use the $518$\,px three-group blend at two-view $0.90$, the deployed score
without its $700$\,px branch. \textbf{(a)} per-site AUROC on the held-out public sites, with and
without the modality-adversarial groups. \textbf{(b)} score by case type: at $\tau=0.94$ the false positive
rate is $0.015$ on clean Normal films and $0.294$ on the $6892$ abnormal films of
